summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, PTSD, bipolar disorder, and prior abdominal surgeries was admitted for worsening pain, nausea, and vomiting due to a new incisional hernia. The hernia was reducible, and imaging showed no bowel obstruction or strangulation. He was managed conservatively with manual reduction, bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control. His diet was gradually advanced, and he tolerated oral intake well. Pain was controlled with transition to oral hydromorphone. He remained stable, ambulatory, and was discharged home with instructions to follow up for elective hernia repair. All chronic medications were continued, and discharge planning included activity restrictions and warning signs to monitor.
